<teammate-message teammate_id="clean-efficiency" color="red" summary="Efficiency review: 7 findings, none severe">
EFFICIENCY review of the uncommitted diff. 7 findings, none severe. Ranked by real cost. No correctness claims.

1. C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\components\DashboardSidebar\providers\ClaudeAccountSidebarProvider\ClaudeAccountSidebarProvider.tsx:122-125
The new `refetchInterval` + `refetchIntervalInBackground: true` polls the roster every 60s forever, including while the window is minimized.
Cost: one host-service RPC plus a provider re-render plus a full memo rebuild every minute with nothing on screen. Minimized for 8h = ~480 needless round trips.
Cheaper: `refetchInterval: () => (document.hidden ? false : SIDEBAR_ACCOUNT_REFETCH_INTERVAL_MS)`, keeping `refetchIntervalInBackground: true`. In Electron a blurred window keeps `visibilityState` "visible" (see ElectronTRPCProvider.tsx:21-23), so this still polls while alt-tabbed, which is the flag's stated reason, and stops only when actually minimized. The focus refetch re-arms it on restore. Repo precedent for `document.hidden`: renderer/lib/terminal/terminal-ws-transport.ts:218.
Caveat: 5 existing queries use the same unguarded pattern, so the diff is in-idiom here. This is an improvement on the house pattern, not a deviation the diff introduced.

2. Same file:135-174
Pace is computed for every account in the roster, but only accounts pinned to a sidebar workspace are ever read (the lookup at 175-184 discards the rest).
Cost: 3 `usagePaceLevel` calls, each with a `Date.parse`, per account per 60s tick. With 8 accounts and 2 pinned, ~18 of 24 parses are thrown away every minute.
Cheaper: derive the pinned-slug set from `states.data` first (it is already needed at 177-181) and pace only slugs in it.

3. Same file:152-171
`account.sevenResetsAt` is parsed twice per account, once for `sevenPace` and again for `fablePace`, because `usagePaceLevel` parses the string internally.
Cost: one redundant `Date.parse` per account per tick.
Cheaper: parse the two timestamps once per account and give `usagePaceLevel` an ms-number parameter instead of a string.

4. Same file:131-133 and the dep list at 187
`statesByWorkspaceId` sits inside the memo whose deps now include `roster.dataUpdatedAt`, so an N-entry Map built purely from `states.data` is rebuilt every 60s even though `states` has no refetch interval and its data has not changed.
Cost: N Map entries rebuilt per minute for nothing, on top of the N new entry objects and the N x 10-field `entriesEqual` diff in `replaceEntries` that the re-pace genuinely needs. N is every visible sidebar workspace on the active host.
Cheaper: split `statesByWorkspaceId` into its own `useMemo(..., [states.data])`.

5. C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\components\DashboardSidebar\components\DashboardSidebarWorkspaceItem\components\ClaudeAccountPicker\ClaudeAccountPicker.tsx:96-128
Each account row re-parses the same two ISO timestamps 5 times. `fiveResetsAt` is parsed by `PctSpan` (via usagePaceLevel:50) and again by `ResetSpan` (via formatResetCompact:68); `sevenResetsAt` is parsed by two `PctSpan`s and one `ResetSpan`.
Cost: 5 `Date.parse` per row for 2 unique values, so 3 wasted per row. Bounded, because the sub-content only mounts on submenu open.
Cheaper: parse both once in `AccountMetrics` and pass numbers down. Same fix as finding 3.
Positive note: hoisting `now = Date.now()` to line 223 and sharing it across rows is the right call.

6. C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\mk-skills\statusline\statusline.py:161 and 182
`_creds_token_sha()` re-opens, re-parses and re-hashes `.credentials.json` on every call, and it is called from both `_read_cache` and every `_write_cache`.
Cost: on the direct-API path (not tray-managed), one statusline invocation goes from 2 credential-file reads to as many as 5, since `get_tray_slug` (line 235) and `fetch_usage_limits` (line 104) already read the same file. Cache-fresh path is +1 read. Tray-managed path is unaffected because `get_usage_limits` never runs. This is a per-statusline-refresh cold-start Python process, so the reads are real syscalls each time.
Cheaper: memoize the sha in a module-level variable (the process is short-lived), or hoist a single `_read_creds()` shared by all four call sites.
Positive note: `_CONFIG_TAG` at line 57 is computed once at module scope. Correct placement.

7. C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\components\DashboardSidebar\components\DashboardSidebarWorkspaceItem\components\ClaudeAccountIndicator\ClaudeAccountIndicator.tsx:81
`usageSlots(account)` runs before the `collapsed` early return at line 83 and before the `state.state === "pinned"` guard at line 94, so a collapsed sidebar and every Following row build the array and discard it.
Cost: one array plus up to 3 objects per row render, and rows re-render on hover, selection and status-dot changes. Negligible in absolute terms; listing it only because moving the call inside the pinned branch is free.

Checked and clean: no long-lived objects capturing large scopes. The `KeyedEntryStore` is created once via a `useState` initializer, the context value is referentially stable so consumers do not re-render on the 60s tick, and `children` keeps its element reference so React bails out of the sidebar subtree. The provider's dedupe via `entriesEqual` is what keeps the 60s re-pace from cascading into row renders, and it works.

REUSE review done (read-only, nothing changed). 7 findings. Two are genuine "an existing helper already decides this" cases; the rest are duplication-cost.

**1. Second Claude-usage colour ramp, different thresholds**
- File: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\apps\desktop\src\renderer\routes\_authenticated\_dashboard\components\DashboardSidebar\utils\claudeUsagePace\claudeUsagePace.ts`, lines 31-35

- Cost: the same account at 85% renders red in the new sidebar chip and amber on the usage page. Two ramps for one concept, in one app, neither aware of the other. Promote one into `claudeUsagePace` and have `UsageView` call it (it needs `bg-*` not `text-*`, so the map wants a tone key with two class variants).

**2. "Reset already passed means 0%" is already defined server-side and is being ignored**
- File: same file, lines 37-46, plus every `formatUsagePct` call site.
- Existing helper: `effectivePercentage(percentage, resetAt, now)` at `packages\host-service\src\claude-accounts\fallback.ts:124` — returns 0 once `resetAt <= now`. It is what the auto-fallback policy uses to decide a pinned account has crossed the tray lines.
- Cost: after a 5h window rolls over but before the Pi refreshes, `usagePaceLevel` colours the stale number green (`timeLeft <= 0` branch) while `formatUsagePct` still prints "97%". The user sees a green 97% for an account the host service already scores as 0%. Fix either by zeroing in the roster mapper (one place, everyone benefits) or by exporting `effectivePercentage` and calling it before display.

**3. `useNow` already exists; the picker hand-rolls a frozen clock**
- File: `...\ClaudeAccountPicker\ClaudeAccountPicker.tsx:223` — `const now = Date.now();` at render.
- Existing helper: `useNow(intervalMs = 1000)` at `apps\desktop\src\renderer\hooks\useNow\useNow.ts:7`, already used by `automations/page.tsx:255` as `useNow(30_000)`.
- Cost: countdowns in an open context menu never tick; they are frozen at the instant the submenu mounted. The provider papers over the same gap a second way, with `notifyOnChangeProps: ["data", "dataUpdatedAt"]` (ClaudeAccountSidebarProvider.tsx:126-128) plus a `roster.dataUpdatedAt` memo dep (line 187) so re-pacing rides on the poll. That is two bespoke clock mechanisms where one `useNow` covers both.

**4. The 5h / weekly / Fable triple is written out three times**
- `...\ClaudeAccountPicker\ClaudeAccountPicker.tsx:94-128` (`AccountMetrics` JSX)
- `...\providers\ClaudeAccountSidebarProvider\ClaudeAccountSidebarProvider.tsx:138-172` (pace join)
- `...\ClaudeAccountIndicator\ClaudeAccountIndicator.tsx:22-34` (`usageSlots`)
- No existing helper to call — this one needs creating. Cost: the "Fable shares the weekly boundary, so pass `sevenResetsAt`" rule is encoded twice in code and explained twice in prose comments (picker 115-116, provider 161-162). Adding or reordering a window means editing three files in lockstep. One `claudeUsageWindows(account)` in `claudeUsagePace/` returning the ordered `{ key, label, pct, resetsAt, windowMs }` triple collapses all three.
- Related: `fableResetsAt` is already fetched and Zod-validated in `packages\host-service\src\claude-accounts\pi-client.ts:218` and lives on `PiAccount` (`types.ts:34`); it is just not on `ClaudeAccountRosterEntry` (`types.ts:18-30`). Adding that one field deletes both substitutions and both comments.

**5. `formatUsagePct` duplicates `formatPercent`** (low)
- `claudeUsagePace.ts:49-51` vs `formatPercent` at `...\TopBar\components\ResourceConsumption\utils\formatters.ts:11`.
- Cost: small and arguably justified — the new one clamps at 999% and shares `displayPct` with the banding, which `formatPercent` does not do. Flagging only so someone doesn't add a third.

**6. statusline.py re-reads and re-parses the credentials file up to five times per render**
- File: `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\mk-skills\statusline\statusline.py:135-149` (`_creds_token_sha`).
- Existing readers of the same file: `fetch_usage_limits()` at line 104 and `get_tray_slug()` at line 235.
- Cost: on the fetch path a single statusline invocation does `_read_cache` (1 read via `_creds_token_sha`), the lock `_write_cache` (2nd), the result `_write_cache` (3rd), plus `get_tray_slug` (4th) and `fetch_usage_limits` (5th) — five `open` + `json.loads` of `.credentials.json`, once per terminal, on every prompt. There is no shared reader; add a module-level `_read_creds()` memoized for the process and have all three call it. The token sha then costs nothing extra.

**7. `format_time_delta` and `formatResetCompact` are the same formatter in two languages** (note, not actionable)
- `statusline.py:88` and `apps\desktop\src\renderer\lib\formatResetTime\formatResetTime.ts:19-42` emit byte-identical strings ("6d17h", "3h12m", "45m", "now"). Nothing to share across the runtime boundary; worth a cross-reference comment in one of them so a future edit to one doesn't silently desync the surfaces.

**Low, mention only:** the provider inlines its own roster `useQuery` (ClaudeAccountSidebarProvider.tsx:114-129) while `useClaudeAccountRoster` exists at `apps\desktop\src\renderer\hooks\host-service\useClaudeAccounts\useClaudeAccounts.ts:52` and is what the picker uses. The inlining pre-dates this diff, but the diff widened it: the shared hook has no polling and the inline copy now has `refetchInterval` + `refetchIntervalInBackground` + `notifyOnChangeProps`. Same query key, so behaviour is fine; it is the config that now exists in two shapes.

**Clean:** the host-service hardening. `BlankedCredentialsError` follows the existing error-class pattern in that module (`WorkspaceLockBusyError` locks.ts:19, `PiRequestError` pi-client.ts:96), `blankedCredentialsSchema` sits alongside `managedCredentialsSchema` in the same style, and the warning plumbing reuses `setWarningCause` / `SILENT_WORKSPACE_CAUSES` rather than inventing a channel. Nothing to reuse that it missed.
</teammate-message>

content.content: @AGENTS.md

## Server-driven announcements (desktop notices)

To show an announcement/warning popup in the app without shipping a release, insert a row in the `desktop_notices` table (served by `GET /api/desktop/version`). Authoring guide — markdown-only body, severities, triggers, targeting, QA previews: `docs/DESKTOP_NOTICES.md`.

## Persisted renderer state (localStorage) policy

Renderer localStorage has one ~10 MB quota, loads synchronously at boot, and keys outlive the code that wrote them — unbounded growth has frozen the renderer before (23.7 MB profile, GH #5496). Every writer must be allowlisted in `src/renderer/lib/persisted-keys/persisted-key-registry.test-data.ts` (CI fails on unregistered writers), and code review must answer three questions:

1. **What bounds it?** A cap/LRU, a TTL, reconciliation against an owning entity, or "fixed-size singleton". "It's small per write" is not a bound.
2. **Who deletes it?** New entity-keyed data belongs in SQLite; existing stores must document their deletion path or sunset plan because deletes from CLIs or other machines can bypass UI cleanup. One-shot payloads must be cleared by their consumer. Deleting a map entry means removing the key, never writing `null`.
3. **What happens when the feature dies?** Move the keys to `DEAD_KEYS` in the same PR that removes the writer; the boot sweep cleans existing profiles. Deleting the writer without registering the key strands it on user profiles forever.

Guardrail: localStorage is for small singleton UI state. Anything entity-scoped with unbounded cardinality, or payloads beyond a few KB, belongs in host-side SQLite (`@superset/local-db` schema, reached over `electronTrpc`) — localStorage collections re-serialize the whole org blob on every mutation. Since #6328 removed SQLite-backed collection persistence, every TanStack DB collection in `CollectionsProvider` is localStorage-backed, so the ~10 MB quota is shared by all of them; `withQuotaGuard`, `notifyQuotaExhausted`, and `evictInactiveOrgs` exist to absorb that pressure and are not a licence to store more.

## Verifying renderer changes via CDP

Read `.agents/skills/cdp-verification/SKILL.md`: attaching to the right renderer, repairing auth, and what counts as end-to-end evidence.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code status line — model, context, API limits, git, 2x promo.

Usage % source: the usage-display Pi feed when the login is tray-managed
(GET /accounts, bearer = push key), direct api.anthropic.com otherwise.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# Force UTF-8 output on Windows
if sys.platform == "win32":
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

# ANSI codes
RESET = "\033[0m"
DIM = "\033[2m"
RED = "\033[31m"
GREEN = "\033[32m"
YELLOW = "\033[33m"
BLUE = "\033[34m"
MAGENTA = "\033[35m"
CYAN = "\033[36m"
WHITE = "\033[97m"
BOLD_RED = "\033[1;31m"
BOLD_GREEN = "\033[1;32m"
BOLD_YELLOW = "\033[1;33m"


def _resolve_config_dir():
    """Where this session's Claude Code state lives.

    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR holds a single literal path — Superset points it at a
    per-workspace profile folder, so each session reports its own account.
    Unset or unusable degrades to the machine-wide ~/.claude.
    """
    raw = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR")
    if raw:
        try:
            path = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(raw.strip()))
            if os.path.isdir(path):
                return path
        except Exception:
            pass
    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".claude")


CONFIG_DIR = _resolve_config_dir()
_CONFIG_TAG = hashlib.sha256(os.path.normcase(CONFIG_DIR).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]

CACHE_FILE = os.path.join(
    os.environ.get("TEMP", "/tmp"), f"claude-usage-cache-{_CONFIG_TAG}.json"
)
CACHE_MAX_AGE = 120
CACHE_JITTER = 60  # random 0–60s added to TTL to stagger terminals
BACKOFF_BASE = 240  # initial backoff 4 minutes, doubles each 429
FETCH_LOCK_TTL = 10  # seconds before a fetch lock is considered stale
CREDS_FILE = os.path.join(CONFIG_DIR, ".credentials.json")
SETTINGS_FILE = os.path.join(CONFIG_DIR, "settings.json")

# Pi usage feed (usage-display add-on). When the login is tray-managed the %
# comes from here — the Pi polls Anthropic once per account, so the statusline
# never hits api.anthropic.com itself (which was getting 429-rate-limited).
PI_URL = "http://100.126.215.29:8126"
PI_KEY_FILE = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".usage-display", "push-key.txt")
PI_CACHE_FILE = os.path.join(os.environ.get("TEMP", "/tmp"), "claude-usage-pi-cache.json")
PI_CACHE_MAX_AGE = 60  # Pi polls upstream every 60s; fresher is pointless
SENTINEL_REFRESH_TOKEN = "managed-by-usage-display-tray"
MANAGED_ACCOUNT_KEY = "trayManagedAccount"


def color_by_pct(pct):
    if pct >= 80:
        return RED
    if pct >= 60:
        return YELLOW
    return GREEN


def format_time_delta(seconds):
    if seconds <= 0:
        return "now"
    days = seconds // 86400
    hours = (seconds % 86400) // 3600
    mins = (seconds % 3600) // 60
    if days > 0:
        return f"{days}d{hours}h"
    if hours > 0:
        return f"{hours}h{mins}m"
    return f"{mins}m"


def fetch_usage_limits():
    """Returns (data_dict, is_429, retry_after_secs) tuple."""
    try:
        with open(CREDS_FILE, "r") as f:
            creds = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None, False, 0

    token = creds.get("claudeAiOauth", {}).get("accessToken", "")
    if not token:
        return None, False, 0

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
            "anthropic-beta": "oauth-2025-04-20",
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=3) as resp:
            return json.loads(resp.read()), False, 0
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        retry_after = 0
        if e.code == 429:
            try:
                retry_after = int(e.headers.get("Retry-After", 0))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                retry_after = 0
        return None, e.code == 429, retry_after
    except Exception:
        return None, False, 0


def _creds_token_sha():
    """First 16 hex of sha256 of the current access token, "" when absent.

    The cache envelope carries this so credentials rewritten in place under
    the same path (an account switch) miss rather than serve the old
    account's numbers.
    """
    try:
        with open(CREDS_FILE, "r") as f:
            token = json.load(f).get("claudeAiOauth", {}).get("accessToken", "")
    except Exception:
        return ""
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
        return ""
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def _read_cache():
    """Read cache envelope. Returns dict with keys: data, backoff_until, backoff_count, fetching_since, mtime."""
    result = {"data": None, "backoff_until": 0, "backoff_count": 0, "fetching_since": 0, "mtime": 0}
    if not os.path.exists(CACHE_FILE):
        return result
    try:
        result["mtime"] = os.path.getmtime(CACHE_FILE)
        with open(CACHE_FILE, "r") as f:
            cache = json.load(f)
        if cache.get("token_sha") != _creds_token_sha():
            # Different token behind the same path — the numbers and the
            # 429 backoff both belonged to the old account.
            return {"data": None, "backoff_until": 0, "backoff_count": 0, "fetching_since": 0, "mtime": 0}
        result["data"] = cache.get("data")
        result["backoff_until"] = cache.get("backoff_until", 0)
        result["backoff_count"] = cache.get("backoff_count", 0)
        result["fetching_since"] = cache.get("fetching_since", 0)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return result


def _write_cache(data, backoff_until=0, backoff_count=0, fetching_since=0):
    try:
        with open(CACHE_FILE, "w") as f:
            json.dump({
                "data": data,
                "backoff_until": backoff_until,
                "backoff_count": backoff_count,
                "fetching_since": fetching_since,
                "token_sha": _creds_token_sha(),
            }, f)
    except Exception:
        pass


def get_usage_limits():
    cache = _read_cache()
    now = time.time()

    # Still within backoff window — return stale data, don't fetch
    if now < cache["backoff_until"]:
        return cache["data"]

    # Cache is fresh (with jitter to stagger terminals)
    jittered_ttl = CACHE_MAX_AGE + random.randint(0, CACHE_JITTER)
    if cache["mtime"] and (now - cache["mtime"]) < jittered_ttl:
        return cache["data"]

    # Fetch lock — another terminal is already fetching

Defect: the roster poll can park permanently-until-next-interaction after a minimize/restore cycle. When the interval fires while minimized (refetchIntervalInBackground: true), query-core re-evaluates the refetchInterval function after that fetch, gets false (document.hidden), and clears the interval (#updateRefetchInterval in queryObserver.js). Nothing re-evaluates it when the window becomes visible again: focusManager (rewired to window focus/blur in ElectronTRPCProvider) only refetches stale queries on focus, and staleTime equals the poll interval (60s).
Failure: minimize for >60s (one background poll fires, interval clears), restore within 60s of that poll while the query is still fresh — no focus refetch, no interval. The sidebar chip's percents and pace colors freeze until the next provider re-render (any sidebar interaction, or the 60s-notifyOnChangeProps path once something else updates the query) or the next blur/refocus after staleness. Self-healing and display-only, hence MINOR, but the "poll resumes when visible" intent stated in the comment is not what the code guarantees.
Fix: subscribe to visibilitychange and call queryClient.invalidateQueries (or refetch) on visible, or drop staleTime below the poll interval so the restore-focus refetch re-arms the interval.
